key_insight: AgentBeats proposes Agentified Agent Assessment (AAA), a unified, agent-agnostic evaluation framework that uses judge agents plus standardized A2A and MCP protocols to improve openness, interoperability, and reproducibility.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical blueprint for benchmarking diverse agent systems without heavy bespoke integration, helping engineers compare agents more fairly across tools, tasks, and deployment settings.
method: Define AAA: judge agents perform assessment while participants communicate through standardized protocols.
Use A2A for task management and MCP for tool access to separate evaluation logic from agent implementation.
Instantiate AAA in AgentBeats with five operation modes to balance openness, privacy, and reproducibility.
evidence_signal: The paper reports a five-month open competition with 298 judge agents and 467 subject agents across 12 categories, plus a coding-agent case study validating fidelity against the public record.
watch_item: Because AAA depends on standardized protocols and judge-agent behavior, real-world adoption may be limited by protocol compliance, governance of judge quality, and privacy constraints in closed environments.
paper_title: AgentBeats: Agentifying Agent Assessment for Openness, Standardization, and Reproducibility
